Divergence 1.5.1 (70)

  • The crash-reporting notice now reaches everyone. In (69) it appeared only on the sign-in screen, so if you were already signed in when you updated, you never saw it. It now appears once, on first launch, whichever screen you land on.
  • If you already decided, nothing asks again. Dismissing the notice, or changing the switch in Settings → General → Diagnostics, is remembered and the notice stays gone.
  • Nothing else in this build changes how a session looks or behaves.

Divergence 1.5.1 (69)

  • Crash reporting can now be turned off. Settings → General → Diagnostics has a working switch. Earlier builds sent crash reports with no way to decline and no indication they were doing it.
  • A notice on first launch says what is sent. Stack traces, your macOS version and a rotating pseudonym — never your name, account, IP address, or a hardware identifier. The notice can turn reporting off directly; it does not block sign-in.
  • What “off” means. New reports stop immediately. A report already written to the offline queue may still be sent once.
  • Nothing else in this build changes how a session looks or behaves. Known, unchanged from (68): in a windowed session the image is still scaled down slightly and looks softest there. Fullscreen is 1:1 and sharpest.
